set -e
SRC="/home/openclaw/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/"
DEST="/home/openclaw/.openclaw/workspace/sessions/"

That satisfies "copy any new or modified .jsonl files". So we can copy all .jsonl from source to destination (maybe using cp -r). Use exec: cp -a. Then perform git commands.

However, we need to ensure git repo exists and has remote configured. Likely there is a git init already.

We can run:

mkdir -p DEST

cp -u (update only when source newer) each .jsonl: cp -u "$SRC"/*.jsonl "$DEST"/

But there are many subdirectories? The source is /home/openclaw/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/. It contains many .jsonl files directly under that dir, not subdirs (just files). So cp -u works.

We'll then cd to DEST, run git add -u (or git add .) then git commit -m "Sync sessions ..." then git push.

Need to get list of files actually copied. Since we use cp -u, it will copy only when newer. We can capture output of cp -vu (verbose). Using cp -vu will print each file copied. Use command: cp -vu "$SRC"/*.jsonl "$DEST"/

Note: the source pattern may expand to many files; we need to handle quoting.

We'll run exec with that command, capture output.

Then run git commands.

Finally report synced files from the cp output.

Let's implement.

arguments.command:
set -e
SRC="/home/openclaw/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions"
DEST="/home/openclaw/.openclaw/workspace/sessions"
mkdir -p "$DEST"
# Copy updated .jsonl files verbosely
CP_OUTPUT=$(cp -vu "$SRC"/*.jsonl "$DEST" 2>&1 || true)
# Change to dest and git add/commit/push if any changes
cd "$DEST"
# Check if any changes
if git status --porcelain | grep -q "\.jsonl"; then
  git add *.jsonl
  git commit -m "Sync session transcripts $(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') UTC"
  git push
fi
# Output copied files list
echo "---COPIED_FILES_START---"
echo "$CP_OUTPUT"
echo "---COPIED_FILES_END---"
